{
  "thinking": "Nobody has picked a picture yet, and the clock is running. A fish is easy to read from its outline if the tail fin is clear, so I'll take the pad and sketch one, with the run starting at the top of the fin and flowing right.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish. The tail fin will sell it. I've got the pad and I'm drawing it now, so you can all see the run before we build.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 7,
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4,6],[9,10],[12,7],[17,6],[21,7],[23,10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[23,10],[21,13],[17,14],[12,13],[9,10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[9,10],[4,14],[4,6]]},
    {"type": "circle", "cx": 19, "cy": 9, "r": 0.6},
    {"type": "label", "x": 5, "y": 4, "text": "tail fin"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Plan: fish facing right. Stroke 1 = fin tip (4,6) -> junction (9,10) -> top body -> nose (23,10). Stroke 2 = nose -> bottom body -> junction. Stroke 3 = lower fin edge (9,10)->(4,14). Stroke 4 needed: fin back edge (4,14)->(4,6), which closes the fin. Eye circle at (19,9). START at fin tip (4,6). Tracing order: 1 first, then 2, 3, 4."
}
